section.title: Activity

para.emphasis: Converting from a Recursive Formula to an Explicit Formula for Arithmetic Sequences

section.para: An arithmetic sequence has the following recursive formula:
Recall that this formula gives us the following two pieces of information:

list.item: To get any term from its previous term, add 2. In other words, the common difference is 2.

section.para: Let’s find an explicit formula for the sequence.
We can represent a sequence whose first term is \(A\) and common difference is \(B\) with the standard explicit form \(A+B(n−1)\).
Therefore, an explicit formula of the sequence is \(a_n=3+2(n−1)\).
section.list:
Write an explicitly (nth term) formula for an arithmetic sequence where \(b_1=2\) and \(b_n=b_{n-1}+7\), \(n\geq2\).
Answer:
\(b_n=2+(n-1)7\)
Converting from a Recursive Formula to an Explicit Formula for Arithmetic Sequences
Now try to take the nth term formula and use it to write the recursive formula of an arithmetic sequence.
We are given the following nth term of an arithmetic sequence:
\(d_n=5+(n-1) \cdot 16\)
This formula is given in the standard explicit form \(A+B(n−1)\), where \(A\) is the first term and \(B\) is the common difference. Therefore, the first term of the sequence is 5, and the common difference is 16.
Let’s find a recursive formula for the sequence. Recall that the recursive formula gives us two pieces of information:

list.item: The first term, which we know is 5.

The pattern rule to get any term from the term that comes before it. which we know is “add 16.”
Therefore, this is a recursive formula for the sequence:
\(d_1=5\), \(d_n=d_{n-1}+16\), \(n\geq 2\).

section.list:
Write the recursive formula of \(e_n=12+(n-1) \cdot 2\).
Answer:
\(e_1=12\), \(e_n=e_{n-1}+2\), \(n\geq 2\)
Converting from a Recursive Formula to an Explicit Formula for Geometric Sequences Now change the recursive formula of a geometric sequence into the nth term.
Here is the recursive formula of a geometric sequence, \(g(n)\):
\(g_1=9\), \(g_n=g_{n-1} \cdot (8)\), \(n\geq2\)
9 is the first term of the sequence, and 8 is the common ratio.
An explicit formula is structured as: \(g(x)=\) (1st term of sequence) \(\cdot\) (common ratio)\(^{(x-1)}\).
Substitute the values, and you get the explicit formula: \(g_n= 9 \cdot 8^{(n-1)}\)

Write the nth term of the geometric sequence where \(g_1=5\) and \(g_n=g_{n-1} \cdot 4\), \(n\geq2\).
Answer:
\(g_n= 5 \cdot 4^{(n-1)}\)
Converting from an Explicit Formula to a Recursive Formula for Geometric Sequences
Finally, geometric sequences represented by the nth term can be represented with the recursive definition.
Start with the nth term formula for \(g_n\) where \(g_n=6 \cdot 3^{n-1}\).
Working backward, when \(n=1\), \(g_1=6\). This is the initial term.
The formula for geometric sequences recursively is \(g_n=g_{n-1} \cdot r\), where \(r\) is the common ratio.
The common ratio of the given sequence is 3.
So, \(g_1=6\), and \(g_n=g_{n-1} \cdot 3\), \(n\geq2\).

list.item: Write the geometric sequence represented by \(g_n=14 \cdot 2^{n-1}\) using the recursive definition.

section.title: 4.18.5: Self Check

para.emphasis: After the activity, students will answer the following question to check their understanding of the concepts explored in the activity.

section.para: QUESTION:
Write the nth term formula of the geometric sequence represented by \(g_1=-3\) and \(g_n=g_{n-1} \cdot 6\), \(n\geq2\).

row.entry: Incorrect. Let’s try again a different way: The common ratio should be raised to the power of \(n-1\), and the first term should be multiplied, not added. The answer is \(g_n=-3 \cdot 6^{n-1}\).
Incorrect. Let’s try again a different way: The first term using this formula is –18. Use \(n-1\) for the exponent. The answer is \(g_n=-3 \cdot 6^{n-1}\).

entry.para: That’s correct! Check yourself: The first term was –3 and the common ratio is 6.

section.title: Switching Between Definitions of Sequences
section.para: A recursive formula defines each term of a sequence using the previous terms.
An explicit or nth term formula defines the terms of the sequence using their position in the sequence, without knowing any other terms in the sequence.

row.entry: \(F_1=a_1\), \(F_n=F_{n-1}+d\), where \(a_1\) is the first term and \(d\) is the common difference.
\(a_n=a_1+(n-1)d\), where \(a_1\) is the first term, \(n\) is the term you want, and \(d\) is the common difference.
\(H_1=a_1\), \(H_n=H_{n-1} \cdot r\), where \(a_1\) is the first term and \(r\) is the common ratio.
\(a_n=a_1r^{n-1}\), where \(a_1\) is the first term, \(n\) is the term you want, and \(r\) is the common ratio.

section.para: Find the explicit general formula for the arithmetic sequence given in recursive form.

Step 1 - Write the recursive formula. (given)
\(a_1=5\), \(a_n=a_{n-1}+6\), \(n\geq2\)

Step 2 - Identify the first term.
\(a_1=5\)

Step 3 - Identify the common difference/ratio.
\(d=6\)

Step 4 - Write the explicit formula.
\(a_n=a_1+(n-1)d\)

Step 5 - Substitute the first term and common difference/ratio into the formula.
\(a_n=5+(n-1)6\)
Check by finding the first 3 terms using each formula:
Both formulas produce the same first 3 terms: 5, 11, 17.
Find the explicit general formula for the geometric sequence given in recursive form.

Step 1 - Write the recursive formula (given).
\(b_1=4\), \(b_n=b_{n-1} \cdot 5\), \(n\geq2\)

Step 2 - Identify the first term.
\(a_1=4\)

Step 3 - Identify the common difference/ratio.
\(r=5\)

Step 4 - Write the explicit formula.
\(a_n=a_1r^{n-1}\)

Step 5 - Substitute the first term and the common difference/ratio into the formula.
\(a_n=4(5)^{n-1}\)
Check by finding the first 3 terms using each formula:
Both formulas produce the same first 3 terms: 4, 20, 100.
Find the recursive formula for the arithmetic sequence given in explicit general form.

Step 1 - Write the explicit formula (given).
\(a_n=21+(n-1)(-2)\)

Step 2 - Identify the first term.
\(a_1=21\)

Step 3 - Identify the common difference/ratio.
\(d=-2\)

Step 4 - Write the recursive formula.
\(F_1=a_1\), \(F_n=F_{n-1}+d\), \(n\geq2\)

Step 5 - Substitute the first term and the common difference/ratio into the formula.
\(F_1=21\), \(F_n=F_{n-1}-2\), \(n\geq2\)

Check your reasoning by finding the first three terms using each formula.
Both formulas produce the same first 3 terms: 21, 19, 17.
Find the recursive formula for the geometric sequence given in explicit general form.

Step 1 - Write the explicit formula.
\(a_n=3 \cdot (\frac14)^{n-1}\)

Step 2 - Identify the first term.
\(a_1=3\)

Step 3 - Identify the common difference/ratio.
\(r= \frac14\)

Step 4 - Write the recursive formula.
\(H_1=a_1\), \(H_n=H_{n-1} \cdot r\), \(n\geq2\)

Step 5 - Substitute the first term and the common difference/ratio into the formula.
\(H_1=3\), \(H_n=H_{n-1} \cdot \frac14\), \(n\geq2\)

Check your reasoning by finding the first three terms using each formula
Both formulas produce the same first 3 terms: 3, \(\frac34\), \(\frac{3}{16}\).
section.title: Try It: Switching Between Definitions of Sequences
section.para: Write the recursive formula for the sequence below that is given in explicit form:
Write down your answer. Then select the Solution button to compare your work.
section.title: Solution
section.para: Here is how to write the sequence using the recursive definition:

Step 1 - Write the explicit formula.
\(a_n=14+(n-1)(3)\)

Step 2 - Identify the first term.
\(a_1=14\)

Step 3 - Identify the common difference.
\(d=3\)

Step 4 - Write the recursive formula.
\(F1=a_1\), \(F_n=F_{n-1}+d\), \(n\geq2\)

Step 5 - Substitute \(a_1\) and \(d\) into the formula.
\(F_1=14\), \(F_n=F_{n-1}+2\), \(n\geq2\)
Both formulas give the same first 3 terms: 14, 17, 20.
